utterances.text: I see you're conversant with these facts, so how many members of the MUP crossed into the basement of that building, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say, but I know that in the building across the way there was a basement where my family were too. And, of course, they talked to the neighbours also at this difficult time where there was destruction and shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You say this occurred in August 1991. Does this mean that members of the MUP and the ZNG, that is between August and November, or rather, you can help us along with this, spent all this time in the immediate vicinity of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the MUP building was hit - it's very difficult for me to be very specific about this - I think it was sometime in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We've heard that already, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it wasn't a case that everybody left the building because the building could still be used despite the damage. As far as I know, the MUP building, too, had a basement. A long time ago, thinking back, thinking back now to a time ago, maybe 30 years ago, there was a prison there in that basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about under that building? Was there an atomic shelter, too?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know. Obviously, I didn't myself go to all the individual parts of the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Which parts did you go to? Because you did say on a number of occasions that you went there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the part that is above the ground, the first door, I think there were two or three entrances. I used the one that was closest to the hospital. I would immediately go to the rooms where the wounded were, those who no longer required hospital treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court about that permit or award, rather, award for cooperation, that you received from the MUP, where you were appointed reserve police officer? Did that bring any privileges to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no privileges at all and it meant nothing really. It was more a token of recognition for going there two or three times, as I said, and dressing the wounds of those people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is that some sort of a thank you note? Is that a decoration that the Croatian MUP awards to people of merit?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how I would describe that. It is just a pass granting no special privilege.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I may be of assistance, did that allow you to obtain weapons?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never had weapons, nor did I ever ask for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you not say that you burned that pass?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my wife. She had it at the time, and she burned everything, all the personal documents, the pass, the passport, as well as the other thing you're asking me about, the reserve police force's ID, as well as the passport and my ID. Perhaps some other personal documents, but I think that's about it. My wife burned all of those alongside with --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you burn?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't burn anything myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you then agree with me that you're now in fact changing a part of your testimony when yesterday you said that you did burn some documents and now you're saying that you didn't?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, it's perfectly simple. You can go back to yesterday's testimony. You can check the transcript, and I clearly stated that my wife did this. If you can go back to yesterday's transcript, you can check my statement, my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's precisely what I did at one point earlier today.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I showed yesterday's testimony to you and my questions were perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: So was my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Your answer was not that your wife did but that you were burning the documents to keep it from falling into the enemy's hands, and today you're telling us that you didn't burn anything at all.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please don't twist my words and don't put words I didn't say into my mouth; this is not something I stated. I talked about my personal documents and keeping it from falling into the enemy's hands. I gave it to my wife, who then proceeded to burn it, burn the whole lot, with the exception of what I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We didn't hear this bit about falling into the enemy's hands, but I will no longer be pursuing this matter, which is of no crucial significance to these proceedings. Can you tell the Court where the x-ray room used to be in the hospital, describe its location.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have the emergency ward, you enter the emergency ward --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a minute, I apologise for this interruption. I move that Exhibit 64 be placed on the ELMO or displayed on the screen; this is the sketch drawn by the witness. We might want to use this to help the witness to provide a more accurate answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. That will be obtained while you carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 65 is the one that has no additions, no markings. Exhibit 65 has no markings made by the witness, no numbers added. Exhibit 65, please. This is an unmarked sketch. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to indicate where the x-ray room was.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you can see me indicating the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the doctor please receive some technical assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please take the marker to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just placed a dot where the x-ray rooms were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to draw a rectangle around that dot?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] It's not very pretty, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We don't have that on the screen, to be quite honest.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want that exhibited?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was going to do it eventually, but we may as well do it now since we started on it. So I move that this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Carry on then, Mr. Borovic, while that is implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Doctor, could you now please use the sketch to indicate the location of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can we see it on this sketch?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's outside the sketch. If you look at the main entrance --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All I was asking is whether we could see it on the sketch or not.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Could you please use the sketch to indicate the location of your room.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which room do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The one that you used in your capacity as a hospital doctor.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not using any single room in the hospital in my professional capacity as a hospital doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the room to the right of the plaster room that you marked the other day? That was not the Crisis Staff room, was it?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean. Doctors sometimes use that room as a meeting room to discuss emergency cases. So that is true, and I placed a dot there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was the Crisis Staff in that room or not?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that was the Crisis Staff room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The room that you marked, were weapons kept in that room at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about when they brought in wounded police officers and ZNG members? Where would they leave the weapons that these wounded members had on them?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When those seriously wounded were brought in -- well, I'll indicate that on the sketch. Here you have the emergency ward, and there is a small room just next to it; you pass it on the way in. There was a pantry there with security. If you turn left or right from there, there are operating theatres, part of the surgical ward. There is one to the left and another one to the right. There is no need to clarify what that means. As soon as the patients were admitted, the security took over their weapons, after which they would leave the weapons here provisionally. And later the weapons were taken to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the security themselves, where did they keep their weapons?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hospital security only had pistols to the best of my recollection. I didn't see any more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So I assume they carried those pistols, if indeed they only had pistols?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to orders received from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many men were armed in the hospital, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say precisely right now, but if you allow me to think it over, I think two or three men in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We talked about the room where Sasa Jovic was. Was there a man, a security, in front of his room?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of this police officer?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Damir Samardzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How long was Damir Samardzic posted outside this room? Could you give us an idea from what time until what point in time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot quite recall when he was posted there first, but I believe this was when they were brought to this room. And I can also show you here on the sketch, because that room is not represented here on the sketch. It is here to the right of the x-ray room. There was a room with a small window up there, and they were here in this room and where -- the part that I am indicating now is where the wounded were. And outside here where I put this dot, that's where the security officer was, to prevent any incidents from occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how long did this guard -- how long was he posted there?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there up until the 20th, the morning of the 20th, when he was taken away together with the other men, put on the buses, and winded up in Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please just mark this first rectangle indicate -- just put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the x-ray room?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then number 2, mark the room where the weapons were held. And with a -- and put 3 where Sasa Jovic was held.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three of them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, mark that room where three JNA soldiers were kept.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were kept there for a while, and then later they were moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the period of time between the 17th and the 20th of November in this x-ray room, did the police leave behind 300 automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. The entire defence did not possess 300 -- the defence of Vukovar did not possess that many weapons. I'm not sure. I don't know for sure. But there were some weapons there, perhaps someone brought a weapon or two there as a provocation, but certainly there weren't that many weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Not that many?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. As I said, this is a room where security guards left their rooms and then they were taken to the police; after all, this was within the competence of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: Was there a guard -- were there security guards outside of the hospital buildings?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there were any.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you don't know, fine. Now, could you tell us where the Elektroslavonija building was?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From here, it was about -- so looking from the hospital it was about 150 to 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that there was firing coming from that building at this period -- in this period of time, would you have any documents indicating that? Do you know that there was any firing coming from that building?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you think I could see anything from the basement, whether there was firing or anything? No, I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now request once a number was assigned to this sketch, because we haven't received that number, for this document which is admitted into evidence, and I move that this document be scanned and then admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could the -- Doctor, could you please mark with a number 4 the position where you said a hospital security guard stood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, next to number 3, which I indicated here, there was a Serbo Chetnik member or members of the Serbo Chetnik JNA. And then below that there was security officers. This is the place where I will -- which I will mark with 4, with number 4. This is where the guard was, the security officer, if I can call him that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that just completed, Mr. Borovic, the record of markings. That document in its present form will be received as the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be Exhibit Number 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope this worked. I hope it wasn't deleted. So I just suggest that perhaps we check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are told, Mr. Borovic, that it will be recovered during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the usher now please show another sketch to the witness, place it on the ELMO? We are done with the old sketch. Could you please adjust that a bit? It's a bit skewed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this sketch?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time that I see this plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I tell you that this sketch was published in your book, and if I were to show this to you, what would your reply to that be?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reply would be that I did see it, but what I meant was this is the first time that I see it as a piece of evidence here because I can even tell you who made the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to that later. My question is this: Are you familiar with this sketch or not because you seem confused just a minute ago. So are you familiar with it or not?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sketch is not part of that portion of the book which was mine, my authorship.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask -- may I ask the usher to show the witness this book again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The question is this: Have you had a chance to see your book, to take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've just seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you see this sketch in the book, including the floor-plan?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is this identical to the one that I showed you which was placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you have just changed your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no -- well, I have to explain how this came to be in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's important to clarify this, to make this more clear. This is something that the editor wanted, and he asked for it, for the floor-plan of the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I'm not trying to confuse you. But just tell me what you can see on the ELMO here, this is the only sketch where you can indicate or put any markings when I ask you questions. So just answer this: Is this sketch that is on the ELMO identical to the sketch that's -- that was published in your book, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the book back, please. Who made this sketch? Who drew it up or who participated in the drawing-up of this sketch?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I tried to tell you a little earlier - and I wasn't really given the opportunity - when I presented my text to the editor, as you can see from the sketch that we were referring to earlier - I'm not very good at this, at making sketches - so at the editor's request, he obtained this sketch, he obtained the floor-plan of the hospital and put it in the book. And I suppose that he obtained this sketch from the architect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who else participated in the production of this sketch?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that this sketch was drawn up by senior nurse Binazija Kolesar, could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's take a look at the sketch. Can you see here the area, because we --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is slightly out of focus, so could you please -- could you please place this in focus for the witness's benefit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the room that is marked with number 10 here?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit -- just give me a moment. I'll have to get --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the ELMO, you will have a clearer view.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is this -- this is my question: Is this room, number 10, was that your office?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the room marked with number 1?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me -- just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: It's right there next to this smaller staircase. Can you see it right there by the entrance and then straight ahead?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was this the room where the Crisis Staff was?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm terribly sorry. I can't see the numbers on the electronic representation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nor can anybody, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Would it be possible for a pen to be used for the room to point at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is the quality of the actual plan that is put on the ELMO or whether the ELMO is out of focus. You're holding something, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I made copies of this. I have copies for the Trial Chamber and my colleagues. The problem is in the focusing. I have a number of copies here, so could perhaps the usher pass them around --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- starting with Your Honours. With Your Honour's permission I would repeat this so that we can all follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So can you see room number 10?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can locate it on the ELMO, but I have to admit that I can't quite point at it here on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you see the list up there in the left-hand corner? Can you see there listed the types of rooms under different numbers?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's very fine print and I have to admit that it puts a lot of strain on my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I help you and tell you that it says there, under number 10, that this is Dr. Njavro's office.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I can say is that whoever made up this sketch obviously thought that I was more important than I actually was because I never spent time, any time, in that room because this was a room for urological patients.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you did not have an office of your own?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Under number 1 it says here that this was the a room where the Crisis Staff was. What is your reply to that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the same. I can say that whoever compiled this sketch or this floor-plan and marked it thus, marked these rooms in this way, this was his arbitrary interpretation, and I don't know how it found its way into the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what room number 20 was. Maybe I can help you out because I am more familiar with this. Under number 20 it says that this was the room of soldier Sasa Jovic.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 20?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, number 26, room 26. Was this the room where Private Sasa Jovic was?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that I'm confused by this sketch. I think it would be easier to point it out at the sketch which I made myself. I have to say that I'm not very good at orientating myself here. I don't even know what part of hospital this is, where it says 27, 28. I have no idea which rooms these are and what part of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just remind you that Binazija Kolesar took part in compiling this sketch, and now you're telling us that it does not reflect reality and that it's not absolutely accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think Binazija Kolesar could never, not then or ever, draw up a sketch like this, although she was a very capable nurse but I don't think she had the technical knowledge to draw up a sketch like this -- although, again I have to repeat, I can't really read this because it's very fine print and although I have my glasses on, I can't really figure out what is where.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Binazija Kolesar is listed at the back of the book as one of the authors of this book, does this mean that she did not take part in the writing of this book or that she didn't put together this sketch or what?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't trying to say that she did not take part in the putting together of this book, but perhaps she was the one who just gave input for this sketch to be drawn up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that the witness did deny some portions or some areas of this sketch, but he did not actually question its authenticity, so I would move to have this admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: We would object.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that it be marked for identification for the time being. Once it's been translated into English, I will move to have it admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, it will be marked for identification. If you have objection, it will considered when the motion is for it to become evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be number 67, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My next question: Witness, when you went to the police building, did you see any radio equipment there?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only stayed in the other room. It was more of a corridor, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you about the radio equipment. So you saw none?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please explain to the Chamber how you sent those faxes, whereas -- well, you actually stated that you did send some. Can you please describe the technical aspects of what you did when you sent those faxes.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never sent a single fax. It was done by a lady called Vera something who was the secretary of Vesna Bosanac. Vesna wrote and sent most of those appeals that were eventually sent to Hotel I and were from there dispatched to the statesmen and politicians all over the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And when you sent yours, what did that look like?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, as I say --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you can't be a bit more specific, how exactly was that done?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I dictated the letters, the substance of the fax messages, and I'm not sure how she sent them, technically speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have one or several Motorolas at the hospital? Did you personally own a piece of equipment like that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no Motorolas, and I had no technical equipment other than what was in this room that you indicated. I'm not sure about the number you mentioned. Can't remember the exact number, but there was a telephone there which was the only telephone which had an open line to the outside world, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the police officers inside the building, did they have Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I didn't look around to see who was carrying what. I had too many other things on my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When there is a problem on the ground and the phone lines are down, and as you said you left the hospital several times, then what happens? Who communicates?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need any communication in order to go and see my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't refer to that sort of intervention, but rather you in your professional capacity as a doctor and the duty you had towards the wounded.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Bosanac is well aware of that. She was in charge of the emergency service. She knows how communication was maintained. I suppose they did have a line that they used to communicate messages to the hospital, and then an ambulance was sent out. Personally, I did not have a Motorola or any mobile piece of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about Dr. Vesna Bosanac, to your knowledge, how did she keep in touch with the outside world?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. She is the one who should answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the number 44560? Who did that number belong to at the time. I know it's been a long time, but please try to think back and remember.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I told you that this was one of the telephone numbers of the Main Staff of the National Guards Corps, would you then remember if perhaps you called them at any time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the National Guards Corps, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You didn't?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't. I'm nearly certain that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Main Staff was, the Main Staff of the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that their headquarters, their Main Staff, was in the former shelter of the former secretariat for All People's Defence of the town of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When were you there?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there only once. I'd been called by the commander known as Mali Jastreb, but that was long before. I think it was early in September. The shelling was not as intense at the time. You could still move about. I went there and asked him to try to secure some ambulances as well as other medical equipment and medicines.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that this paramilitary formation supplied some medical equipment to you or medical supplies?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I did ask and I don't think it's a paramilitary unit. That's one thing. Secondly, as defence commander, together with the other Jastreb, I assumed he would have been well-placed to request assistance from Zagreb. They had arrived from Zagreb to try to secure some medical supplies at least so that we could help the wounded. The number of the wounded group on a daily basis gradually.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far was that Main Staff from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps just over 300 metres, but it's a rough assessment. I didn't exactly measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you agree with me if I say that it would have been much simpler for you to walk the few metres to the MUP building, since as you said the ZNG were under the control of the Croatian MUP or, rather, the police station? What was the reason behind your decision to run the risk of being seriously injured just to cross that open area?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we misunderstood each other. Your Honours, I need to explain what the competence of the MUP was. Pursuant to an order from Zagreb, Jastreb 1 and Jastreb 2 arrived in Vukovar in late August 1991. They were there, and we were told when they arrived in the hospital that they were the ones who would take over the defence of Vukovar. They were a logical choice to go and speak to when medical supplies needed to be secured, whatever was necessary, whatever was indispensable in order to administer assistance to the wounded and sick.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this mean that back in August, Stipe Polo had superiors whose names were Jastreb 1 and Jastreb 2? That's my first question. For the benefit of the Chamber, Stipe Polo was the police commander, wasn't he, the police chief in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the police commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that he was subordinated to Jastreb Mali and Jastreb Veliki?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't concern myself with the military police hierarchies at the time. It wasn't up to me to think about those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's try to solve this little riddle, shall we? What was Jastreb 1's name and what was Jastreb 2's name?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one's name was Mile Dedakovic, and the person known as Jastreb Mali was called Borkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What sort of relations did you have with Borkovic nowadays?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Friendly in a distant way. Nothing special. I haven't seen him in a long time, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mladi Jastreb, is he a physician by profession?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know. I think he had completed the military academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So how should I take your answer when you say that you are friendly in a distant kind of way? You're not colleagues. Am I to take it to mean that or you both worked for the police? How am I to understand that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I think you're confusing a number of things there. I was a student of the classics, after all, so when I say "colleague," I mean friend. When I say "colleague," I mean friend. I didn't mean colleague as a fellow doctor. Among lawyers, you must after all address yourselves as colleagues, which doesn't necessarily mean that you all have a Ph.D.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You do know that Mladi Jastreb was a policemen of the MUP and you were a reserve officer of that same MUP. I thought it was on that basis that you continued your cooperation, but now that you've clarified this point, I believe we can move on. My next question: What was the distance between the municipality building and the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 250 or 300 metres. 300 would be a more accurate estimate, and the command was right next to it, the distance between perhaps 20 metres not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This command or headquarters that is only 20 metres away from the municipality, did this building have an underground shelter? You were there once, after all.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there once, but I didn't go around the building. I just went there to help the wounded and drove straight back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you were there, is there a staircase leading to an underground area?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is an underground area in the building, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any radio equipment when you were there?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't. To be quite honest, I didn't, but I did see a telephone. Like anywhere else, I didn't have time to look around. There was a lull in the shelling, and it's a well-known thing that during the shelling of Vukovar there would be lulls every once in a while lasting one or two hours. And all those who needed to go somewhere had to dash right off. Some people, unfortunately, lost their lives because they miscalculated the time required to get somewhere. They had to hurry, they had to rush, seize the time, and the same applied to me. I had no time to look around. I just had to rush straight to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you sometimes go to that room to administer medical assistance to a colleague of yours?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because in October the shelling became heavier, 50.000 shells fell, so it was no longer possible -- even if I had been flown there in a space rocket, it would have been difficult for me to reach that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since you said you have a problem and are in a hurry to go back for these festivities, please try to keep your answers brief. Keep it down to yes or no, wherever possible.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I will try to be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the members of the ZNG held any prisoners in the municipality building?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that I heard. An injured man came along named Alfred Hin [phoen] and told me that they were being treated in a fair manner. Logically, I asked who those people were. He told me that they were being treated in a fair and proper manner. However, I can't rule out the possibility just like I protected those people in the hospital, that somebody may have done something that was not proper or fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When did this man named Alfred tell you that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the first half of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what eventually became of them, since I see that you know something about it?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because I left myself. You know precisely where I was taken to, to the camp; therefore, I was no longer in a position to know what had become of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: With this officer named KOS [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this officer but there was another officer, a major, and a lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Court building is in relation to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if at any point in time wounded ZNG or police members were brought from that building to the hospital, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any wounded being brought over from the court building, but as I said, we were pressed for space in the hospital. And those patients or wounded who no longer required daily hospital care were taken there, but I don't remember the reverse being the fact, that somebody was beak brought in from the court building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So who was it who drove those people, the ZNG members and members of the police, to the court building and which route did they take?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: People would come from the police. I'm not talking about the ZNG. I'm talking about the police only.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When was this now that we are talking about, this bit of information?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime in October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was anyone watching them there?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, there are police members inside the court building, it's wartime. Were there any armed people guarding them? I think that's a perfectly reasonable question.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say the court building. I said they were, the wounded were, in the police building. So as soon as they were in the police building, there was no need for anyone to watch over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The confusion may be yours, Doctor, with all due respect. I was asking you about the court building.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But all the while I was talking about the police building and I'll say this again. The police building only, although next to it was a building that belonged to the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So were there any of those members in the court building?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since I see that you went around the police building and the headquarters building, at least on one occasion, did you know in which buildings around Vukovar members of the ZNG and the police were staying, in addition to these buildings already known?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In answer to what I think was a question by my learned friend from the OTP, you said that the hospital was hit on the 6th of August and you had to move to the gynaecology ward.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the operating theatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You also testified there were no patients in the gynaecology ward at the time and that was the reason you went there.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The operating theatres were free. There were patients in the ward, but the theatres themselves were not being used at the time. A birth room is one thing and gynaecologial surgery is quite another. Excuse me, I needed to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You have sufficiently clarified it, but you said there were no patients there. I do accept your present answer, though. I think you said that the shelling stopped on the 17th of November in its entirety. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th, I said. The 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Altogether?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was no longer any shelling on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was no shelling at all on the 18th or the 19th?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The hospital was no longer being targeted?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th, 18th, 19th and 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The hospital was not being targeted?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether on the 17th, 18th, or 19th, Dr. Vesna Bosanac sent out any of the appeals that we discussed?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't categorically confirm that but I assume, based on my recollection, that she sent the last one out on the 17th or the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to tell you now, since the OTP agrees with me on this, I'm quite positive about that, there is no need to make you read telephone-recorded messages or faxes that constitute these calls for help by Mr. [as interpreted] Vesna Bosanac in which she literally states that on the morning of the 18th, at 10 past 10.00 in the morning and 1540 hours in the afternoon the hospital was shelled and hit. Does this mean that the appeals that were sent out did not reflect - please mind my question because it's very carefully worded - that the facts reflected in these appeals were false or erroneous, simply untruthful?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I say that that's what the appeals state, that on the 18th the hospital was shelled three times, my question is: Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, as I've stated repeatedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but we have evidence I thought that Dr. Bosanac sent off the faxes on the 18th and that related to her personal knowledge. I wasn't aware that she said that she did it with Dr. Njavro. Dr. Njavro can give evidence from what he knows from his personal knowledge, but he cannot, in my submission, do anything more than speculate on the basis of what the -- what has been called the appeal but the fax was on the 17th, 18th, or on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, that last question didn't relate to that. The question was whether the hospital -- whether it is true or not that the hospital was shelled on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I accept that entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I say something otherwise it might be too late?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Moore is suggesting an answer to the witness because I am in the process of cross-examination, and this explanation actually may be even suggesting an answer and it's not permissible to do that. I didn't mention that Dr. Njavro is mentioned in these appeals at all. I just wanted to test the assertions by a witness as well as an exhibit that was admitted here, whether it's true or not. We've done this with other witnesses. Mr. Moore wasn't there on that day. Perhaps he didn't see when the witnesses were reading these faxes and telephone messages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I thank my learned friend for his customary courtesy. My point and my submission is quite simply this: That if may well be that o other people have said that the hotel was hit three times, four times, six times, ten times but that has to do with their personal knowledge. All this witness can be asked is: From your knowledge, do you say this hospital was hit or not? And if so, how many times? It goes to the state of knowledge of the witness. He cannot be asked in relation to the state of the knowledge of another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm grateful to counsel for their ongoing assistance, but can I go back to the last question which Mr. Borovic put? It is a proper question and the witness may be able to answer it. And that question, Doctor, was whether it was -- is true or not that the hospital was shelled on the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember, because I was still performing surgeries on the 18th, and I was in the hospital. The last person I operated on was a 3-year-old child. I don't remember if there was shelling. I really was focused on something else. So if there were any shells, I really don't remember whether there were any on the 18th, 19th, or the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If Your Honours permit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Earlier you said the 16th, the 17th, 18th, and the 19th you said that there was no shelling of the town and the hospital. Do you abide by that statement?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said on the 16th I was still performing surgeries, so I abide by what I said. I didn't hear the shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm not ruling out the possibility, perhaps in relation to those who were not so involved in their work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My note of the previous answer was the 17th, 18th, 19th, and 20th, not the 16th. I think the witness's answer has dealt with that sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You are absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many members, family members, of employees of the hospital were staying at the atomic shelter?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't give you an exact number. I don't want to speculate. Dr. Ivankovic's family was also there. Also the families of some other colleagues, doctors, also nurse Stanko Vujanovic -- actually the sister of Stanko Vujanovic was also there. There were also lots of nurses whose husbands were brought and children brought in over the last days. So I really couldn't tell you exactly how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I didn't ask you about the last few days. You already mentioned that many people came in that period. But during the time up until the 17th of November, before the Yugoslav People's Army came, there were the employed doctors, the nurses, the aids also. So were the family members of those employees there at the hospital in that period?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shelling every day. A large number of shells were falling, so it was not possible even to blink without seeing or hearing a shell fall on the hospital or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The answer -- the question was very simple, yes or no. We've already heard about the shelling.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to clarify and I will tell you yes or no. The nurses could not go home in such conditions to see to their families, to their children, their husbands, in order to make it easier for them to stay at the hospital and work better, without too much fear about their near and dear ones, it was possible. And, of course, Dr. Bosanac would know that better because she approved that and we all agreed with that at the hospital, because there were doctors also whose family members were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So can you finally give us the answer, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So approximately how many of these people were there?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you I couldn't really give you an exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was it over a hundred people?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think it was such a large number of persons. It's difficult that there was -- to say that there were so many people in that one room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But do you allow the possibility that there could have been so many family members?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really couldn't agree with you about that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Slightly fewer people than --

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fewer but I couldn't give you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's make a test. Where was the husband of the hospital director during that time? If I were to tell you that he was at the front and that he was a member of the ZNG, would you believe that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know, and I don't think that he was in the National Guards Corps because when the windows and the window frames were destroyed, everything was destroyed, he tried to close that up as much as he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Dr. Vesna Bosanac's sons were? Were they in the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that one son was in the National Guards Corps, but he was seriously wounded. His -- he had sustained injuries to the eyes and to some other parts of his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So one of the sons was in the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but very briefly. So you wouldn't really even consider him having been a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about Dr. Neda Striber, was her husband in the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know that. I don't even know his name. And I don't know if Striber is her maiden name or her last name by marriage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to go through every single point, but perhaps you can give me an answer to the following questions. Were most of the husbands of the hospital employees members of the National Guards Corps and were most of their children outside of the -- outside of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were most of the husbands of the female hospital staff members of the National Guards Corps, and were they -- their children at that time outside of Croatia and outside of Vukovar in any case?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know, but I don't believe so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there sporadic electricity and water cuts, and was this power and water supply restored from time to time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. This happened but then we switched to generators.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I wasn't there. I didn't go near it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: There is a part of the statement -- of the book which I will not ask you to read out because it may not be a part that you authored, but it says that the electricity was at some point restored to the barracks. Whether this is true or not can be subject to discussion. But the question is: Who would be in the position to turn electrical power and water on or off?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I assume that that was under the jurisdiction of the government representatives. I don't know who would be turning the electricity and water on and off.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was the commissioner at the time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. Marin Biling [phoen], but I don't know who was turning the power on and off, who was the one who would be issuing orders to that effect. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that he could appoint somebody to do that, he didn't have to do that himself; I'm talking about the commissioner.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many JNA tanks were destroyed during the war operations?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know the exact number, and I wouldn't want to speculate about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The allegations in your book, are they real allegations or are they just speculation?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are real, they are something that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from those who were defending Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: For example, who did you hear things like that from?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, I heard -- I heard from -- something like that from Petar Janjic, Tromblon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear something about the JNA, and if you did, who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was also something that I heard from the defenders of Vukovar, but I really don't know who it was anymore. You really have to take into account that quite sometime has passed since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have enough men to defend Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I know how many people would be sufficient to defend Vukovar? I am something different. I'm a doctor, and this is what I was doing. I don't know how many people would be required to defend Vukovar, but I did hear from those who were involved in that how many there were but I don't know how many would be needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us how many there were?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to what I heard at the end and this is something that Mladi Jastreb, Branko Borkovic, stated, so according to him, there was a total of 2.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: A total of 2.000 defenders?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And these were all members of the MUP and the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court if there was a joint command or a command to encompass Vinkovci, Vukovar, and Zupanja?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that in your book this is mentioned and that you did talk about this in your book, does that mean that you received this information from someone else?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I did, but once I left. So we are talking about the time in Vukovar. Vukovar is the topic and the time period is something that we are talking about now and not about the period after that, so it's probably something that I heard about after I left Vukovar and after the camp. I really don't know who the commander was, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you know there was a joint command, and you found out about that later?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where was this command located? What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assumed if it was a joint command, it was located in Vinkovci but I only assumed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm or do you know that Mladi Jastreb was frequently in phone contact with Dr. Vesna Bosanac or are you -- do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to trouble you too much by citing sections from the book, but if I were to tell you - and this is something that you can check - that it says in your book that Mladi Jastreb was frequently in telephone contact with Dr. Bosanac, what would you say to that? How did you get that information?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably from Dr. Bosanac because I was at the hospital with her, but you will allow me to say that time had its effect. So I don't know how often they were in telephone contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you allow for that possibility?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's possible, but I really don't know whether that was so or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the president of Croatia was at that time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Franjo Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if he came to Vukovar in July 1991?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in mid-July he did come to Vukovar, and as far as I recall, he came to the centre of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who did he see? What did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he met the commissioner. I assume that. He was a person in charge, a person of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who was the Croat -- Croatian prime minister at the time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, but I'm not quite certain. It was a long time ago, and there were many prime ministers in the interval, but I think it was Mr. Josip Manolic. I'm not sure though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, you made a mistake. It was somebody else. But my question was: Do you know if this prime minister visited Vukovar in August?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. As far as I can recall, he did, although I didn't have any contact with him whatsoever, but I think that he did visit in August. He did visit Vukovar in August. And I think that the Prime Minister was Mr. Josip Manolic, but I could be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are wrong. Do you know whether Franjo Greguric came to Vukovar -- actually the prime minister was Franjo Greguric?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This was on the 8th of August 1991. Do you know that after that, there was a special measure introduced in Vukovar with special passes being in effect, the ZNG introduced its own passes for Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was some talk about special passes and that one needed to report to the Main Staff or to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Report to whom or where?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was either to report to the municipal building or maybe to the people's defence secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was heading the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, the head of the secretariat - and this was in late summer - was Tomislav Mercep.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And what was his relationship with the military police and the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us, if you know, what these special passes were used for, which the citizens of Vukovar were supposed to use?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know. I didn't need one so I didn't use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you use the police pass that you had?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you misunderstood me. I got my police pass much later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean in August?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, if we are talking about August, I got it in September.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So that was 15 days later?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was almost a month later. I think it was during Greguric's visit, if my calculations are correct, and I think I can still do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In your book it says on the 18th, but we won't dwell on that. But the gist of my question is as follows --

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This pass, which restricted movement, was that something that every person needed in order to leave Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, but I think that that was its purpose. But I really don't remember enough details in order to be able to answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Two JNA planes were downed. You said -- well, I'm not going to ask you about that. When you heard that two JNA planes were downed, my question in relation to that is: On that day, did the ZNG members block Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. You would need to ask that at the ZNG command. I really don't know. I don't have information about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I would then like to draw your attention to your book on page 18, where it states that -- well, I will give you the book. I don't want to appear to be manipulating you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher kindly show the book to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said page 18 or 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. This is on page 18. Top of the page. So start reading from the top.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just one moment. I need to clarify something. These were a text that were copied from the HINA news agency. This has nothing to do with my thoughts. This is just conveying the daily reports by HINA. These are not my reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course, I support that. That's also the position of the Trial Chamber. But would you confirm that it states in that text that on the day that the two planes were downed the ZNG had blocked Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that say that in the text? It's at the top.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Very well, at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: It's about five lines down from the top.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The ZNGs blocked Vukovar. Military vehicles are not allowed to move around. The only secure road is Vinkovci, Nustar, Mankrinci [phoen], Bogdanovci."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But as you simply conveyed the media report, this is not your standpoint?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's nobody's standpoint. It's information published by the public media. I'm certainly not the author of this, nor did I keep a diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to turn to page 176, and then I won't trouble you with the book any longer. So this is my last point to do with the book.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to read the caption underneath the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 176?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, underneath the photograph. It says: "In the fighting for Vukovar."

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said underneath the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to the text below the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the fighting for Vukovar 104" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] " -- 400 fighters and MUP members were killed as well as 700 citizens of Vukovar who died of shelling. The enemy losses according to Croatian information is at least 6.000, according to foreign sources 8.000."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any comment on this part of the text in your book that 6.000 to 8.000 JNA soldiers were killed?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot assert that. This is simply what we heard and what international media reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you try to verify this before putting it in your book?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably took this from reputable newspapers abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean you believed this information?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot assert categorically anything about it, whether I believed it or not. I simply conveyed there information, just as I conveyed the information about the number of those killed in Vukovar up to the point in time when we registered those numbers for both sides but actually more people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As this is how it is, I will now ask you to read the last sentence of this text, the same text. And then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During the war, 2500 wounded were treated in Vukovar Hospital and the number of those who died was" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: As this was information which would be well-known to you, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there is also the clinic in Borovo Komerc which took care of a certain number of wounded, so the total number is higher than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think the number of 80 did not enter the record, so I would like it to be entered into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That 80 died in the hospital. Thank you. I think maybe it's time for a break. It's up to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic and I, Mr. Borovic, each thought you were saying it was your last question. Our hopes rose, but not so. We will adjourn now and resume at five minutes past six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Coded signals. Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It is, actually. Your Honour, just to assist the Court, we have had an opportunity of discussing various matters outside. The Court is aware that there is a memorial service this week in Vukovar. The doctor has expressed very clear view that he would like to return tomorrow for those services for his own personal reasons. We were working out the timings. Mr. Lukic, I think -- I don't know if he's the one who is actually doing the cross-examination, but whoever is doing it on behalf of Mr. Sljivancanin will be eloquent and I suspect will take, from what I understand, three to four hours. That being the case, if the Court is agreeable, what counsel propose is that the cross-examination ceases this evening at the end of Mr. Radic's cross-examination, that the doctor then is allowed to go home and returns to court at a date that is mutually convenient for all parties for the final part of cross-examination and re-examination. Now, I for my part, on behalf of the Prosecution, am happy with that particular position. I believe I'm right in saying that all the Defence are equally agreeable to that course. But clearly it's subject to the decision of the Court. We merely air it for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it would have the advantage of allowing the doctor to leave to be -- to go home tomorrow. Is that a course that would be preferable to you, doctor? I see you nodding yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We express our appreciation to counsel for their finding of this solution. That gives you a little more freedom, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before I begin putting questions, I wish to have an error in the transcript corrected. On page 66, line 10, where it says, "With this officer whose name is Kos," it should say, "with this KOS officer." "KOS" is not a name of a person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, during those three months, how many ZNG members you treated and how many members of the police?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it's stated at the end and as I read out before the break, in the Vukovar Hospital, apart from Borovo, Borovo Komerc, there were about two and a half thousand wounded who were treated. The information as to how many of these were civilians and how many members, I was just about --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I was asking you about ZNG members.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just about to say that. We have to be precise. And for the sake of the truth we have to say how many were civilians, how many members of the ZNG and how many were members of the MUP, the police. But I really don't have this information. I do know, however, that the ratio of civilians to ZNG and MUP members was some 65 to 70 per cent in favour, unfortunately I have to say, of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that if you don't have the information?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the information that sticks in my mind from the book, while we were keeping track of this information until the end of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that we can get this information through the books that were kept, the records, that is?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those that were gathered up and taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the term "Ustasha" means?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
