utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I've heard the term and I know what it means. I have even been called that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What have you been called?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people called all Croats Ustasha. If they were calling all Croats Ustasha, then that must include myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And you personally?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that some have called me, personally, that on entering the hospital, but I cannot say that anybody hit me or physically maltreated me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what do you know about the Ustasha? Who are they?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The history of the Ustasha movement is something I have really not studied, and how the Ustasha movement developed I'm not competent to provide correct information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you complete secondary school?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is there a subject called national history in secondary school?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my time, and this was around 1959, in the late 1950s, we did study history, whether the name of the subject was national history I couldn't say or general history or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you had a subject called history in school?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And what kind of marks did you have as a pupil in secondary school?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was a very good pupil, not to exaggerate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you must have had very good marks in history, I assume?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I had very good marks, yes, not excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: As you had very good marks - Their Honours and I know less about this - who were the Ustasha forces, according to what history says? Did they belong to the fascist forces in World War II or were they antifascists? You must have learned that lesson.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's easy to answer. They did belong to the fascist bloc, not the antifascist bloc. That was a completely different bloc.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you then explain why you, who are obviously of an antifascist orientation, would have been called a Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have to ask those who called me that name, not me. I don't know the reason. I don't see any reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sremska Mitrovica, you were taken there?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You say that you made a statement there. Did you write it in your own handwriting?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you give it of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say now after entering --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you don't want to speak about that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. The military court in Belgrade, I've already touched on that.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I have an additional question about it. You said there was a judgement.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A judgement was never handed down, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But there was a trial.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How many judges participated? You remember, you were sitting in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one judge sitting across from me, to the right was a court reporter, to my right was a counsel, and to my left the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. As my colleague Mr. Domazet also asked you about this, you said: No, there was no investigation, there was a trial. I have to tell you now: Do you agree - I'm not trying to teach you - but do you agree that for the crime of armed rebellion, the mandatory sentence is ten years or more? And in all trials there are always Trial Chambers consisting of three to five judges. Do you agree that this was the case in Croatia before and now?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with court procedure, but why would all those people have been there around me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that this was an investigation, not a trial proper, because in a trial proper there is a Chamber of three judges or, in cases of more serious crimes, of five judges. As there was no panel, would you agree that you were never actually tried but that you were simply heard once by an investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because then I would have been there on my own. What would I have to do with an investigating judge? At that trial, I had counsel, a captain, I don't know what his name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I do know he was a captain and I think he was in the air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. So there was one judge?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So this could not have been a trial proper. Let's leave it. If I tell you that there can be no proper trial heard by only one judge and without an investigation phase before that, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can neither agree nor disagree. What I'm telling Their Honours is what it was like and how I was treated in that court. I felt that it was a trial, and that's why I'm saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How many times were you questioned, only once?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the statement that we have, the only one you signed, is that the statement you gave? You signed only one statement in the military court?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never signed any statement in the military court, at least to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that you signed only one statement, and I believe the statement was invoked by the OTP. It's a signed statement, and I will show you the statement now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, do you want to see a copy of that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is that your statement? Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to look at it more closely. This is a photocopy, and some of these look like my signatures. In some places my signature appears to be missing. Some pages appear to be half signed. In order to be able to confirm your question, I would have to go through the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Please do so. I got this statement from the OTP, just for you to know. Have you had enough time?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this statement? You might want to keep it for the time being. Do you remember this statement?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that I was questioned, but I can't remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please give the statement back to the doctor. I have another question. Can the usher please give the statement back to the witness. We are in the middle of cross-examination here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can we see your signature at the bottom of these pages, with the exception of page 1, which is the official part?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at page 2, please? Does it say, "investigating judge"?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you now believe me that this was an investigation, not a trial, now that you've seen this?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe you, although up here it says "military court in Belgrade," and that may be why I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we then agree that there was no trial, merely an investigation?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. I would like to have my copy back, please. I asked you these questions because you stated in chief that you had been acquitted. I wanted to show this to prove that all that ever happened was an investigation. There was no trial. You had already been exchanged and the proceedings were suspended. However, you are not a suspect here or an accused. This is a mere circumstance that I wish to present to the Chamber. At the beginning of his examination-in-chief, Mr. Moore very much emphasised the fact that you were being held in detention with no foundation at all and that you were later released.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never stated that I was released. I was clear about this. I was exchanged and proceedings had been afoot against me, but no decision was ever handed down. No indictment was delivered and no acquittal was delivered.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That appears to be the correct answer. Can you please tell us: What does the expression "battalion" mean?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "battalion" in Croatian would mean, roughly speaking -- just a minute, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is that a brigade, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that might be a bit too big in terms of size.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So it's smaller than a brigade?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, smaller. I think it comprises about 100 soldiers, roughly speaking, at least based on what I heard in my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you know how many battalions there were at the Vukovar front?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that this is something that's in your book, but we are not going into that because information is available on this. The 1st Battalion was at Sajmiste, the 2nd was as Mitnica, the 3rd and Borovo Lusac, and the 4th in Vukovar and at Novi Bogdanovci. Would that information be consistent with the fact, such as they were on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this was written by Mladen Sreb [phoen]. I think he was the one who wrote this. You should be asking him, not me. He's responsible for that bit of information, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We've dealt with this book quite extensively. You must understand that the Defence had to deal with it because of this late information that you provided the OTP with. Why did you not state that there were other people who authored the book alongside with you? Because many people seem to have been involved in the making of this book.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about my co-authors. Well, when the book was written we wanted to inform the public about what had happened in Vukovar. Mali Jastreb was not the only one who wrote this. There was another one of the commanders or defenders, I'm not sure, from Sajmiste or Mitnica. I think Sajmiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Stjepan Sucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please place this on the ELMO? It's a map. We will have this on the screen, so I'm not sure if it's necessary to distribute copies. There appears to be no reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the map?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but before you ask any questions, counsel, I must say this is a military map. I would be hard put to interpret or read this military map. This was enclosed and perhaps drawn by Branko Borkovic, Mali Jastreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Branko Borkovic?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Branko Borkovic. He knew all the operations and he headed the Vukovar defence and quite competently, if I may add.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If you could please put this on the screen so that we can all see it, I accept that Mali Jastreb was the one who drew this. And there is an index at the top of the map. Blue means Croatian forces, red means the aggressors' forces. Isn't that what it appears to say?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that blue colour used to mark the Croatian forces surrounds in their entirety places such as Vukovar and Borovo Naselje, and there is an uninterrupted line leading to Vinkovci and Bogdanovci. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I mean the blue line. These are the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that, but what I don't understand is the road being open entirely to Vinkovci and Nustar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Let's take one thing at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could have the map back on the screen, please, so that I can follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Let's tackle this portion where it says "Vukovar" and "Borovo." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see both.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Danube?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does it not appear to be surrounded on all sides by Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not surrounded by Croatian forces, but surrounded by the JNA forces on both sides, both banks of the Danube, you can see it quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But this section of the map showing Vukovar and Borovo, do we see a line here marking the positions of the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I should be interpreting this, not being a military person myself or a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The witness has said this is not his map, that he would have difficulty interpreting it. I can certainly understand questions about red and blue, but if it is one step further, again to try and interpret the military element, I have two objections. One, it's not his map; and two, he does not have the expertise or the knowledge on the evidence that he's given at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, everything you say is correct, but I don't think that Mr. Borovic has reached that point yet. So we will carry on and see whether we do go too far or stay within this witness's capacity to deal with questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm doing my best not to ask any provocative questions or answer -- or ask any questions that the witness might be in no position to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So my question is: Do you not see that around Vukovar and Borovo there are blue markings or lines signifying the Croatian forces, according to the index that we see at the top of the map?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's only in as far as I can interpret this military map, drawn by an expert. I'm a layman in these matters. I know nothing about these matters. I know, since you've told me, that these forces that were marked in blue are surrounded on all sides by the forces marked in red on both banks of the Danube, as well as other areas belonging to Vukovar municipality. The blue troops seem to be fully surrounded in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You see this map is dealing with the situation as it was in the second half of October 1991.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The 19th?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And the movement of the first humanitarian convoy on the 13th is also recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm just by looking at this map, without going into any military interpretations, being as you are just a witness who happened to be in Vukovar at the time, can you agree with my assertion that the Croatian forces to a large extent held the area of Vukovar and Borovo under control?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is not the entire area of Vukovar. It's not Vukovar in its totality. There is an area of Vukovar here that is outside the control of the National Guards Corps or the police for that matter, such areas as Petrova Gora and part of Sajmiste. This can be seen clearly on the map. It's a sizeable area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since you seem yourself to have ventured into a military interpretation, can you please indicate Petrova Gora and Sajmiste on the map because I can't see these.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying this because I'm familiar with the area, and I know where things are. When you go from Vukovar to Negoslavci, this is the area referred to as Petrova Gora, and further east in the general direction of Belgrade, if you like, is -- rather, if you go towards Negoslavci, you will find Sajmiste. And over here in the direction of Petrovci, where the Ruthenians lived, were the prevailing ethnic group, is a section of Vukovar which is on a high ground and it belongs to Fruska Gora or Mount Fruska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My last question on this subject is: Were Croatian forces comprehensively in control of Vukovar, Borovo, and Sajmiste at the time under consideration here, the time that the map shows?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, if you look at Vukovar itself, because outside Vukovar Lipovaca and part of Borovo also belong to Vukovar, but for the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Another question that I forgot, which will be my last question: On the 19th of November, when the army, as you said, exchanged the reservists, do you remember if those soldiers were wearing white belts?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who among them was wearing what, unless they declared themselves as JNA members, as some others declared themselves as members of the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the JNA. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember what sort of belts they were wearing. I really don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified in chief that only specific surgeons were able to operate on human organs and use them for transplants and for organ trafficking.

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can take the example of Croatia now. In Croatia at present there is only one team qualified to do that sort of thing. The others don't venture into that area. When needed, they extract organs in compliance with all the laws of medicine. This is a special skill and a separate profession really, and then they take it elsewhere, wherever it's needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of yourself as an expert, which I am certain of, but do you have the skill required to do this?

utterances.speaker: JURAJ NJAVRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This was not meant to taunt you, but it's just that the Prosecutor asked certain questions about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I decide to call it a day. This may not be the most convenient time for me, but I must take other things into account as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Mr. Lukic? Are you wanting to continue now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We are ready to go. That's no problem at all. We might start now. There is another thing that I wanted to ask. Please don't think that I'm now going into something that is normally up to the Chamber, the Chamber's responsibility and the Chamber's duty. But please, since the witness is being released, could you caution the witness of his duties, the duties that are incumbent upon him once he leaves this courtroom? We know that the witness will probably have an opportunity to meet other witnesses in the meantime before he returns. I have just gone through the manual on the protection of victims and witnesses. I have seen no provision governing that situation, and I am aware of what the duties of a witness are when a testimony is interrupted. Therefore, I would kindly ask the Chamber to caution the witness about these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As the cross-examination by you, Mr. Lukic, may not continue until some unpredictable time in the future, I think it would be preferable for us to break now and allow you to make a clean start whenever it resumes. So we will now adjourn. Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness leaves the Court, I would submit that the Defence have not cross-examined in the way that's laid down in Rule 90(H)(ii) where what is said is quite simply this: "In the cross-examination of a witness who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party, counsel shall put to that witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears, which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness." In my submission, what has not been done so far is as follows: It has not been put to the witness whether in actual fact he disputes or that on behalf of Captain Radic it's disputed that there was any meeting with Dr. Njavro on the 18th; if there was a meeting with Dr. Njavro on the 19th; whether in actual fact there was a removal of Aric on the 19th and the return of Aric, which I believe was on the 20th. Those are specific allegations against Captain Radic. In my submission, the Rules are perfectly clear on that, and my learned friend is beholden to let the witness have an opportunity to reply to that. And indeed the matter should be clarified for the Court and the Prosecution's benefit. And as I say, the Rules are mandatory, not discretionary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore. You want to respond now, Mr. Borovic? I was going to say that the Chamber would give you time to reflect on that, and if you felt there was anything further that you should put to comply with the rule, you could do that when you resumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I thought, Your Honour, but for the sake of facts, I never mentioned Aric myself. It was an example of improper conducts by the Defence, but that was not actually right. But I will reserve the right to respond to this, if there is a need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, it's not a matter of you reserving right, but once you've had an opportunity to consider your cross-examination, before the witness returns, if you conclude that to comply with the rule, which is clear and mandatory, that you need to put some other matter to the witness, you might apply to the Chamber then for leave to do so. Doctor, as you've gathered, we are now going to adjourn, with a view to you being able to return as you wish to Vukovar for the balance of this week. At some time in the future that fits in with the time-table of this trial and your own affairs, you will be asked to return to complete your evidence. If you would bear in mind that during that break, you should not discuss your evidence or the circumstances relevant to this case with any person, that will avoid you and others encountering potential difficulty. You should simply indicate, if somebody wants to talk about the case, that you are in the course of giving your evidence and you are not free to talk about the evidence with anybody else. And you most assuredly should not talk to other witnesses in this case about your evidence. With those words of advice and caution, we will now adjourn to resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of November, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.45 p.m.,
